rules.why: Commits go through the harness: after a passing verify, run('steps', 'step_done', {plan, message}); it checks the plan's change and commits its files itself.
Stage files by name (git add a.py b.py), never everything: -A, --all, . or :/ can pick up secrets and files no plan names.
The repository's own hooks always run: take --no-verify (or commit -n) out.
git reset --hard throws uncommitted work away: keep it (git stash) or restore one file with git restore <file>.
History on a remote is never rewritten: no --force, -f, --force-with-lease, --mirror or +refspec. Push new commits instead.
A protected branch (project.json protected; main and master by default) is never written from here: work on a branch of the plan and open a merge request.
The home, the repository that holds the harness, never pushes; its changes are released by the maintainer.
Agent files (.claude/, CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md) never reach a remote: unstage them, or take them out of the commits to push.
git with a global option the gate does not follow (-c, --git-dir, --work-tree...) may run in another repository or skip its hooks: the user is asked.
